Crispy Vegan Honey Garlic Tofu

This crispy Vegan Honey Garlic Tofu is sweet, savory, garlicky, and just spicy enough. Crispy seasoned tofu gets tossed in a sticky garlic sauce with fresh ginger, sriracha, onions, and whole chiles for an easy plant-based dinner that tastes like takeout at home!

Vegan Honey Garlic Tofu

I haven’t been able to stop thinking about honey garlic chicken since watching the latest season of Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars. In episode three, one of the chefs was working on a honey garlic chicken dish, and since then, the sweet, savory, garlicky combination has been living in my head rent-free. So, naturally, I had to make my own version. This vegan honey garlic tofu is my answer to that craving. It’s crispy, sticky, sweet, savory, loaded with garlic and fresh ginger, and has just the right amount of heat. I use agave instead of honey, but if you consume honey or have a vegan honey you love, that’d be ideal.

If you love crispy tofu (or if you’re a tofu skeptic) and anything involving a sticky, garlicky sauce, I have a feeling this one is going to become a favorite!

Jump to Recipe

Why You’ll Love This Recipe

  • Budget-friendly and accessible ingredients: A 16-ounce block of extra-firm tofu costs roughly $3-4 at most grocery stores, making this an affordable dinner option compared to meat-based takeout alternatives. And ingredients like garlic, onions, cornstarch, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and soy sauce are common items you might already have on hand!
  • Ready in less than 30 minutes: From pressing tofu to plated, this meal is ready in about 25 minutes. So much faster and cheaper (and better!) than waiting for food delivery.
  • Beginner tofu-friendly: Many first-time tofu cooks struggle with soggy results or bland seasoning. The cornstarch coating and air-frying guarantees crispness, and the bold sauce is a favorite! This is the perfect recipe for those who are just starting to cook tofu.
  • Impressive with minimal effort: Guests assume you ordered takeout until you mention it’s homemade. Looks restaurant-worthy despite basically being throw-together meal.
  • Perfect weeknight dinner:  Active time is under 15 minutes with hands-off air frying. You can prep vegetables or set the table while the tofu crisps. Perfect for busy weeknights!
Jump to Recipe
Jump to Recipe

Step-by-Step Instructions

1. Prepare the Tofu:

Preheat air fryer to 400°F. Press tofu, then tear into 1½-inch cubes. Toss with 1 tablespoon cornstarch, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper until evenly coated. Arrange in a single layer in the air fryer basket and cook 15 to 20 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden brown.

2. Whisk the Sauce:

Whisk remaining 1½ teaspoons cornstarch with vegan broth. Add agave, soy sauce, minced garlic, rice vinegar, sriracha, ginger, and sesame oil. Set aside.

3. Sauté Aromatics:

Heat neutral oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add diced onion and Thai chiles, sautéing until translucent, 2 to 3 minutes.

4. Simmer:

Pour the sauce mixture into the pan and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low, stirring occasionally, until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes.

5. Combine, Serve and Enjoy!

Add crispy tofu to the pan and toss to coat evenly in the sauce. Serve over rice, garnished with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green onion. Enjoy!

Tips and FAQs

  • Pressing the tofu: Wrap the block in paper towels or a clean kitchen towel, place a heavy pan on top, and let sit 15 to 20 minutes. Excess moisture prevents crispiness.
  • Tearing vs. cubing: Torn pieces have more surface area than uniform cubes, helping the sauce cling better!
  • Don’t overcrowd the air fryer: Arrange tofu in a single layer with space between pieces. Cook in batches if necessary. Crowding can lead to steam instead of crispness.
  • Sauce consistency test: When the sauce coats the back of a spoon and you can drag a line through it with your spatula, it’s ready! It only takes a few minutes.
  • Keep the chiles whole: Leaving Thai chiles whole infuses heat without making the dish too spicy. Remove them before serving if desired.
Jump to Recipe

Do I have to use an air-fryer?

You can bake the tofu at 425°F for 25 to 30 minutes or pan-fry it in neutral oil until crisp, though the texture varies slightly.

How do I store leftovers?

Keep tofu and sauce together in an airtight container for up to 3 days in the refrigerator. Reheat in a skillet to restore crispness.

Can I make the sauce ahead of time?

Yes, the sauce stores for up to a week refrigerated. Warm gently and add a splash of broth if it thickens too much.

Crispy Tofu + Sticky Garlic Sauce = Dinner Solved

If you’re craving takeout but want quicker, cheaper and more delicious, this vegan Honey Garlic Tofu needs to be on your list! The tofu is crispy around the edges, the sauce is sticky, savory and sweet, the garlic and ginger are bold, and the whole chiles add just enough heat to keep things interesting. Serve it over steamed rice or noodles, spoon plenty of that sauce over the top, and enjoy!

Vegan Honey Garlic Tofu

Ashley
This crispy Vegan Honey Garlic Tofu is sweet, savory, garlicky, and just spicy enough. Crispy seasoned tofu gets tossed in a sticky garlic sauce with fresh ginger, sriracha, onions, and whole chiles for an easy plant-based dinner that tastes like takeout at home!
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 20 minutes mins
Cook Time 25 minutes mins
Course Lunch/Dinner, Main, Main Course
Cuisine Chinese-American
Servings 4
Calories 207 kcal

Ingredients
  

  • 1 (16-ounce) block extra-firm tofu, pressed and torn into 1 ½ – inch cubes
  • 1 tablespoon + 1 ½ teaspoons cornstarch, divided
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
  • 1 teaspoon pepper, plus more to taste
  • ¼ cup vegan chicken broth or vegetable broth
  • ¼ cup agave or vegan honey
  • 2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce
  • 8-10 cloves fresh minced garlic
  • 1 tablespoon seasoned rice vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon sriracha
  • 2 teaspoons fresh minced ginger
  • 2 teaspoons toasted sesame oil
  • 1 tablespoon neutral oil, such as avocado or canola
  • 1 yellow onion, diced
  • 3-6 whole Thai red chiles
  • Cooked rice, for serving, optional
  • Toasted sesame seeds, for garnish, optional
  • Green onion, for garnish, optional

Instructions
 

  • Preheat your air-fryer to 400°F.
  • While that’s preheating, place the tofu in a large bowl and sprinkle in 1 tablespoon of the cornstarch, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Toss until thoroughly coated.
  • Arrange the tofu in a single layer in your air-fryer basket, making sure not to overcrowd it (you may need to do this in batches depending on the size of your air-fryer). Air fry at 400°F for 15 to 20 minutes, tossing or shaking the basket halfway through, until the tofu is golden brown and crisp around the edges. Set aside.
  • In a small bowl, whisk the remaining 1 ½ teaspoons of the cornstarch with the vegan chicken broth. Add the agave, soy sauce, minced garlic, rice vinegar, sriracha, minced ginger and sesame oil. Whisk once more to combine and set aside.
  • Heat the neutral oil in a large sauté pan or wok over medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, add the onion and Thai chiles and sauté, stirring often, until the onions are translucent, 2 to 3 minutes.
  • Pour in the sauce and bring to a simmer.
  • Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue to simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes. Taste and adjust seasonings, adding more salt and pepper if necessary.
  • Add the crispy tofu and toss to coat in the sauce.
  • Serve over rice, garnish with toasted sesame seeds and green onion. Enjoy!
